name: Roman Empire
hook: Forums, gladiators, emperors and the long decline — the empire Jeopardy never stops excavating.

facts.label: Edward Gibbon
facts.statement: Edward Gibbon wrote The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, published in 1788; it later landed on the Vatican's Index of Forbidden Books.

facts.label: the Byzantine Empire
facts.statement: The Byzantine Empire was the Eastern Roman Empire; it outlasted the Western empire by nearly 1,000 years, with its capital at Constantinople.

facts.label: Constantine
facts.statement: Constantine issued the Edict of Milan in 313, legalizing Christianity, and in 330 moved the imperial capital to Byzantium, which became Constantinople.

facts.label: Attila the Hun
facts.statement: Attila the Hun — the Latins' Flagellum Dei, or "Scourge of God" — attacked the Roman Empire in the 5th century and forced the Eastern empire to pay him gold yearly.

facts.label: the forum
facts.statement: The forum was ancient Rome's marketplace and civic center, the equivalent of the Greek agora; the Tabularium, or state archives, stood there.

facts.label: gladiators
facts.statement: Gladiators were trained arena fighters who fought to the death for public entertainment; the word comes from gladius, Latin for sword.

facts.label: provinces
facts.statement: At its height the Roman Empire ruled provinces from Britain to Egypt; Egypt became one after Cleopatra's death in 30 B.C.
